title: Local weak equations and symbols for real metric bundle differential operators
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], use a smooth real $m$-manifold $N$ without boundary [def-sfb-smooth-real-manifold], smooth rank-$q$ real vector bundles [def-sfb-smooth-real-vector-bundle], and their actual smooth sections [def-sfb-smooth-bundle-sections]. Package a metric bundle by these existing bundle structures with smoothly varying positive definite real fibre inner products. An orientation is a covering subatlas of the maximal smooth atlas with positive transition Jacobian determinants. A smooth positive volume is a measure $\mu$ whose pushforward in each atlas chart $c$ is $\rho_c\,dz$ on its target, with $\rho_c$ smooth and strictly positive. Use the dependent almost-everywhere $L^2$ classes and ordered real multi-index derivatives of [def-sfb-bundle-sobolev-space]; this is the same $L^2$ definition for any specified measure $\mu$. For metric bundles $G,H$ of rank $q$, put $V_p=c_p(U_p\cap U^G_p\cap U^H_p)$, where $c_p$ is the chart at $p$ and $U^G_p,U^H_p$ are its preferred frame domains. For a section $s$, write $s^G_p$ for its coefficients in these coordinates. A smooth differential operator of order at most $k$ consists of a real-linear map $Q:\Gamma^\infty(G)\to\Gamma^\infty(H)$ and smooth real matrices $b_{p,\alpha}$ on $V_p$, for $|\alpha|\le k$, such that $(Qs)^H_p=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k} b_{p,\alpha}\partial^\alpha s^G_p$ for every smooth section. Define its degree-$k$ symbol by $\sigma_k(Q)(p,z,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=k}b_{p,\alpha}(z)\xi^\alpha$, and ellipticity by invertibility for all $p$, $z\in V_p$ and nonzero real $\xi$. For $u\in L^2(G,\mu)$ and $f\in\Gamma^\infty(H)$ define the weak equation $Qu=f$ by, for every $p$, output component $a$, and compactly supported smooth real test $\phi$ with closed support inside $V_p$, $$\int_{V_p} f^H_{p,a}\phi\,dz=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\sum_b(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{V_p}u^G_{p,b}\,\partial^\alpha(b_{p,\alpha,ab}\phi)\,dz.$$ Use the chosen representative of the existing dependent quotient in this identity. Define having a smooth representative by existence of a smooth section equal almost everywhere to that representative. On a smooth positive volume these formulations are independent of the representative and express equality of the corresponding local coefficient distributions; no global distribution or operator map is chosen from an existence theorem.
